EUSurvey 1.6 Missing Authorization via Questionnaire PDF Invitation Check

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4ff1ba0, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the GET /pdf/survey/{surveyId} endpoint that allows attackers holding a valid invitation for one survey to download a different survey's restricted questionnaire PDF without signing in. PDFController checks that the supplied invitation and participation group are active but not that they belong to the requested survey, exposing questions intended only for invited respondents of any published survey that allows PDF access.
EUSurvey 1.6 Blind SSRF via PDF Export

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 03cc974, contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability in PDF export that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to make the server send HTTP or HTTPS requests to internal services. Question titles saved through POST /{shortname}/management/edit are rendered as raw markup in runnercontentinnerpdf.jsp, and the PDFRenderer resource loader fetches referenced images without checking whether the destination is on an internal network when a response is exported as a PDF.
EUSurvey 1.6 Insecure Direct Object Reference via exports/checkNew

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 6db6147, contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the GET /exports/checkNew endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to read the names of other users' finished exports and suppress their notifications. ExportsController trusts a user ID supplied by the browser without checking it against the authenticated session, and ExportService marks every export it returns as notified, so the owner never receives the notice that their export is ready.
EUSurvey 1.5.2-1.6 Stored XSS via Delphi Explanation Field

EUSurvey 1.5.2 through 1.6, prior to commit bb7432c, contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Delphi survey explanations that allows survey participants to execute arbitrary JavaScript in other users' browsers. Explanations submitted to POST /runner/delphiUpdate are stored by AnswerExplanationService without sanitization and rendered as HTML in delphiAnswersTable.jsp, so an injected event handler runs in the EUSurvey origin with the session of any participant or survey manager who views the answers table.
EUSurvey 1.6 Authenticated Blind SQL Injection via Dashboard Sort Parameter

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4bf95a3, contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the GET /dashboard/surveys endpoint that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to infer data from the main application database. SurveyService inserts unrecognized sort values directly into the ORDER BY clause of a native query, so attackers can supply SQL expressions and use response timing to infer any data readable by the application's database account, including data outside the surveys listed on their dashboard.
EUSurvey 1.5.2-1.6 Missing Authorization via delphiUpdate Endpoint

EUSurvey 1.5.2 through 1.6, prior to commit ffd5da7, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the public POST /runner/delphiUpdate endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit responses to Delphi surveys after the owner has closed them. DelphiController checks only that the survey exists and is a Delphi survey and skips the closure check enforced by the normal survey page, so an attacker who knows the survey and question IDs can create new responses that remain in the survey's results.
EUSurvey 1.6 Unauthenticated Contribution Overwrite via Edit Endpoint

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit de1145c, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public POST /editcontribution/{code} endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite another respondent's submitted answers. The handler in ContributionController selects the survey and answer set from body parameters by numeric contribution ID and never checks that the private edit code in the URL matches that contribution, so an attacker who knows a contribution ID can replace its saved answers without the respondent's edit link.
EUSurvey 1.4.4.6738-1.6 Unauthenticated SQL Injection via Public Result Filters

EUSurvey 1.4.4.6738 through 1.6, prior to commit de1145c, contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the public results page GET /publication/{shortname} that allows unauthenticated attackers to infer non-public response data. ReportingService builds a SQL column expression from part of a user-supplied filter parameter name and inserts it directly into the query, so a visitor to any survey that publishes its results can inject boolean conditions and use the presence or absence of public result rows to infer private reporting data, including response data and respondent metadata from other surv
EUSurvey 1.6 Authorization Bypass via preparepublishedcontribution Endpoint

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4bf95a3, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the GET /preparepublishedcontribution/{id} endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to read private responses submitted to published surveys. The contribution PDF handler in ContributionController looks up a response by its sequential database ID and skips the normal response access checks, so attackers can enumerate IDs to retrieve other respondents' answers, including free-text answers that may contain personal data, across surveys.
EUSurvey 1.6 Incorrect Authorization via Contact-Share Handlers

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit edb5021, contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the GET /settings/shareEdit/{shareId} and POST /settings/shares handlers that allows any authenticated user to read or modify another user's contact share. The ownership check in SettingsController denies access only when a condition is both true and false, so it never denies access, allowing an ordinary account without Contact Management privileges to read the names and email addresses in a share and to rename it, change its recipient or access mode, or replace its contacts.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 118facd, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public POST /runner/draft/runner endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite another participant's saved draft and obtain its private invitation token. EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit a4161a9, contains a weak password recovery mechanism that allows attackers who obtain a still-valid password-reset link to take over accounts that use a local EUSurvey password. The /auth/reset/ flow checks only the age of a reset code and does not invalidate it after the password is changed, and issuing a newer link leaves earlier links active, so a used or superseded link remains valid for up to 24 hours from issuance and can be reused to set a new password, sign in as the affected user, and lock that user out.
EUSurvey 1.5.5-1.6 Missing Authorization via bulkchange Endpoint

EUSurvey 1.5.5 through 1.6, prior to commit d5295d5, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the POST /forms/bulkchange endpoint that allows any authenticated user to take over or delete other users' surveys. SurveyController accepts arbitrary survey IDs and privilege values, and BulkExecutor applies the requested access-right changes or deletion without checking whether the requester can manage those surveys, allowing an ordinary ROLE_USER account to grant itself full control of another user's survey, read its draft and results, edit the form, manage its invitations, or delete it.
EUSurvey 1.6 Path Traversal RCE via importSurvey

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 0669a36, contains a path traversal vulnerability in the survey import function that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to execute arbitrary code on the server. The POST /noform/management/importSurvey endpoint trusts archive entry names when SurveyExportHelper writes imported files through FileService, so a crafted survey archive can write a JSP file outside the survey storage directory into the application directory, where Tomcat executes it with the privileges of the EUSurvey process

Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: group-admin deny bypass via top-level group move

A flaw was found in the administrative interface of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when Fine-Grained Admin Permissions are used to restrict a group administrator from managing specific sub-groups. DreameHome before 2.6.4.0 Code Integrity Bypass via RnPluginDownloadManager

Attackers can replace both the downloaded bundle and its corresponding MD5 metadata to run modified code with the application's permissions and access to its bridge APIs.
DreameHome MQTT Broker Improper Authorization After Share Revocation

Assimp through 6.0.6 Infinite Loop via Collada ReadPrimitives Index List

Assimp through 6.0.6 Uncontrolled Memory Allocation via FBX Rotation Keyframe Interpolation

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in FBXConverter::GetRotationKeyframeList that allows attackers to exhaust memory via unbounded rotation angle differences. Attackers can supply a crafted FBX file of about 111 KB whose keyframe interpolation loop never advances, consuming gigabytes of memory until the importing process is killed.
Assimp 6.0.0 through 6.0.6 Infinite Loop via Comment Line in SkipLine

Assimp 6.0.0 through 6.0.6 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in SkipLine that allows attackers to hang parsing by supplying files with '#' comment lines. Attackers can provide crafted OFF, LWS, or MD3 shader files so ReadFile never returns, consuming a CPU core and denying service.
Assimp through 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Read via Collada CopyVertex

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ColladaParser::CopyVertex that allows attackers to read heap memory by supplying primitives lacking a VERTEX input. Attackers can provide a crafted Collada file whose SIZE_MAX per-vertex offset bypasses the release-removed ai_assert check, crashing the importing application.
Assimp through 6.0.6 Uninitialized Resource Use via glTF 1.0 Strip/Fan Faces

Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file whose strip or fan primitives trigger out-of-bounds reads or null pointer dereferences, crashing the importing application.
Assimp through 6.0.6 Invalid Pointer Dereference via glTF 1.0 Embedded Image

Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with an embedded image mime type lacking a slash to crash the importing application.
Assimp through 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Read via glTF 1.0 Accessor Counts

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that uses NORMAL and TEXCOORD accessors without comparing their counts to the POSITION vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with shorter normal or texture coordinate arrays to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads and writes that crash the importing application.
Assimp through 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Write via glTF 1.0 Accessor Element Size

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in glTFAsset.inl that allows attackers to corrupt memory via oversized glTF 1.0 accessor elements. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with VEC4 position or VEC3 index accessors to overflow heap or stack buffers during import, crashing applications.
Assimp through 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Read via Collada ReadFloat

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ReadFloat in ColladaLoader.cpp because accessor stride and offset bounds are checked only by ai_assert. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose animation accessor describes more values than its float_array holds to read past the array or dereference null, crashing the importing application.
Assimp through 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Write via PLY Importer Face Indices

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in PLYImporter::LoadFace and PLYImporter::createFromeTriStrip that fails to validate face vertex indices against the vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file whose out-of-range indices cause GenVertexNormalsProcess::GenMeshVertexNormals to write normals outside the heap buffer, crashing the application or potentially enabling code execution.

Attackers can send POST requests to /api/v1/archives/<linkId> to replace another user's stored screenshot, PDF, readable, or HTML archive with attacker-supplied content.
Weblate before 2026.11 Account Takeover via Unicode E-mail Matching in Password Reset

Weblate before 2026.11 contains an account takeover vulnerability in the reset_password view that allows unauthenticated attackers to reset victim passwords by abusing case-insensitive Unicode e-mail matching. Attackers controlling a lookalike mailbox using a dotless i or other case-folding variant receive the victim's reset link, since it is sent to the typed address, and set a new password.
Frappe before 15.126.0 and 16.x before 16.55.0 Prototype Pollution via Dashboard Chart custom_options

Frappe before 15.126.0 and 16.x before 16.55.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows Dashboard Manager users to pollute Object.prototype by storing __proto__ keys in Dashboard Chart custom_options. When any user, including administrators, views a dashboard rendering the chart, Object.assign merges attacker properties into Object.prototype, altering Frappe desk client behavior for that session.
Dashy 4.0.0 before 4.9.12 Credential Disclosure via isLocalRequest Prefix Check

Dashy 4.0.0 before 4.9.12 contains a credential disclosure vulnerability in isLocalRequest that attaches user credentials to lookalike hosts due to prefix-only origin checks. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a crafted ?config= link pointing to a lookalike host, capturing bearer tokens or HTTP auth headers to read configuration and stored API keys, or modify them when the victim is an admin.
Langfuse before 4.82.0 SSRF via GitHub Enterprise SSO baseUrl

Langfuse before 4.82.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows organization admins to target internal hosts by setting the GitHub Enterprise SSO baseUrl, which skips outbound-URL validation. Attackers can point baseUrl to loopback, RFC1918, or cloud metadata addresses so user sign-ins trigger server requests carrying stored OAuth client credentials.
Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 Path Traversal via Nextcloud Provider get_file

Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in Nextcloud.get_file that allows authenticated recipe editors to write and delete files by using unsanitized recipe names in temporary paths. Attackers can set a recipe name containing ../ segments via PATCH /api/recipe/<pk>/ and request /api/get_recipe_file/<pk>/ to overwrite and remove .pdf files outside the temporary directory.
RSSHub before 2026.11.01-8521.e529e9b Credential Exposure via javdb Domain Validation Bypass

RSSHub before 2026.11.01-8521.e529e9b contains a domain validation bypass in the javdb routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to capture the operator's JAVDB_SESSION cookie. Attackers can pass an absolute javdb.com URL in the category parameter and set the domain query to a host they control, causing processItems to send the _jdb_session cookie there.
Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 tagsecure Bypass via Escaped URL in Tags File

Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 contains a security bypass vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers to evade 'tagsecure' URL checks by escaping URLs in tags file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw fetch an attacker-controlled URL leaking environment variable values.
Chatwoot before 4.20.0 Information Disclosure via Public Help Center Article Endpoints

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read unpublished help center articles through the public portal API. Attackers can request archived articles by slug via the ArticlesController show actions or read draft translations exposed through associated_articles in article JSON responses.
Casdoor before 4.27.1 Denial of Service via SAML Message Decompression

Casdoor before 4.27.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in decodeSamlMessage that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory by sending unbounded DEFLATE-compressed SAML messages. Attackers can send a small, highly compressed SAMLRequest or SAMLResponse to the /api/saml/logout/:owner/:application endpoint, which inflates to gigabytes and crashes or stalls the server.
Umami 3.3.0 before 3.5.0 2FA Bypass via Race Condition in /api/2fa/verify

Umami 3.3.0 before 3.5.0 contains a race condition in two-factor authentication attempt limiting that allows attackers holding a user's password to bypass lockout. Attackers can send many concurrent POST requests to /api/2fa/verify that pass checkRateLimit before recordFailedAttempt runs, brute-forcing TOTP or backup codes beyond the five-attempt limit.
Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.19.1 Stored XSS via SVG Sanitizer Re-serialization

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.19.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the sanitize-svg function that allows authenticated users to bypass filtering through unescaped re-serialization. Attackers with file edit permission can upload SVGs using entity-encoded or CDATA-wrapped markup or attribute quote breakouts to execute JavaScript in the Penpot origin when victims open them.
Lightdash before 3.212.0 Credential Exposure via AI Writeback GitLab Read Access

Lightdash before 3.212.0 contains an insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability in getGitlabInstallationRepoReadAccess that sends the organization GitLab app token to unverified hosts. Project developers can set the dbt connection host_domain to an attacker-controlled server and capture the token when the AI agent reads the repository, gaining access to every reachable repository.
erxes before 3.4.14 Missing Authentication via insurance_api Contract Template Mutations

erxes before 3.4.14 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the insurance_api plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to create, overwrite or delete contract templates via GraphQL mutations. Attackers can inject HTML into templates rendered by headless Chromium during generateContractPDF to pull internal network content into PDFs and exfiltrate customer fields.
Gradio 6.27.0 before 6.32.0 Authentication Bypass via Forged Host Header

Gradio 6.27.0 before 6.32.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in gradio/history.py that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to use the operator's locally saved Hugging Face token by sending a forged Host: localhost header. When ssr_mode is enabled, requests proxied through the local Node SSR server pass the loopback check, letting attackers call run history endpoints to list buckets, read records and assets, and write buckets under the operator's account.
Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.98 Link Following via .actrc --eventpath

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.98 contains a link following vulnerability that allows malicious repositories to read host files by setting --eventpath in an untrusted project .actrc to a symlink. Attackers can commit an event.json symlink pointing to files like ~/.ssh/id_rsa, which act copies into the job container as GITHUB_EVENT_PATH for workflow steps to exfiltrate.
Kitty 0.43.0 before 0.51.0 Terminal Escape Injection via choose-files Preview

Kitty 0.43.0 before 0.51.0 contains a terminal escape sequence injection vulnerability that allows attackers to emit escape sequences by crafting malicious file or archive member names. When a victim highlights such an entry in the choose-files kitten preview panel, unsanitized names are written raw, enabling OSC 52 clipboard overwrites, OSC 8 links, window title changes, or screen spoofing.
Sustainsys.Saml2 before 1.0.4 and 2.x before 2.11.1 Improper Signature Verification via HTTP-Redirect Binding

Sustainsys.Saml2 before 1.0.4 and 2.x before 2.11.1 contains an improper signature verification vulnerability that allows attackers to tamper with signed parameters by exploiting mis-parsing in CheckSignature() of Saml2RedirectBinding.cs. Attackers can append data after an extra '=' in RelayState of an intercepted or replayed Redirect-binding message, causing applications to trust the tampered value.
Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 Memory Exhaustion via ASGI HTTP/1 Parser

Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the pure-Python ASGI HTTP/1 parser that buffers protocol lines without size limits. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send request lines, headers, chunk-size lines or trailers lacking CRLF to grow worker memory and consume CPU, causing denial of service.
Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 HTTP Request Smuggling via ASGI Python Parser

Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in the pure-Python ASGI parser that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to desynchronize request framing by sending malformed framing headers. Attackers can send whitespace-padded Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length headers, signed Content-Length values, or invalid chunk terminators to smuggle requests past front-end proxies to the ASGI application.
Delta Sharing Server 1.4.0 before 1.5.0 Incorrect Permission Assignment via Azure SAS Tokens

Delta Sharing reference server 1.4.0 before 1.5.0 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows share recipients to read unshared data via container-scoped Azure SAS tokens. Recipients with a valid bearer token can request credentials from the temporary-table-credentials endpoint to read every blob in the storage container, including unshared tables.
oasdiff 1.24.0 before 1.34.1 External Reference Policy Bypass via --open

oasdiff 1.24.0 before 1.34.1 fails to enforce --allow-external-refs=false when --open is used, because the recordingReader() capture reader in load/capture.go never applies the external-reference policy. Attackers supplying an untrusted OpenAPI spec can use external $ref values to read local files or trigger HTTP requests, with contents uploaded in the review bundle.
mcp-server-kubernetes before 4.2.0 Argument Injection via Flag-Shaped Positional Operands

mcp-server-kubernetes before 4.2.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows remote MCP clients to inject kubectl flags by supplying dash-prefixed values as positional operands in tools such as exec_in_pod, kubectl_patch, and kubectl_logs. Attackers connected over SSE or Streamable HTTP transport can supply values like --filename to make kubectl read files from the server host, bypassing file-read restrictions.
sigstore-js @sigstore/oci before 0.8.0 Credential Exposure via Cross-Origin Redirect

sigstore-js @sigstore/oci before 0.8.0 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that leaks registry credentials by replaying OAuth2 password-grant request bodies on cross-origin 307 or 308 redirects. Attackers who can make a trusted token service redirect to their host via open redirect or compromise receive the username and password POSTed by RegistryClient.
simple-git before 4.1.0 Argument Injection via --exec Option in ls-remote

simple-git before 4.1.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the allowUnsafePack guard by supplying the --exec option to non-push git operations. Attackers who influence arguments passed to listRemote() or raw() can inject --exec for ls-remote, archive, fetch-pack or send-pack to execute commands on the host.
binary-parser before 2.3.1 Code Injection via String-Typed Parser Options

binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption(). Attackers can supply crafted length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() alias values to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled.
Faye websocket-driver 0.5.0 before 0.8.0 Decompression Bomb via permessage-deflate

Faye websocket-driver 0.5.0 before 0.8.0, permessage-deflate before 0.2.0, and websocket-extensions before 0.2.0 contain a decompression bomb vulnerability because messages are fully inflated before maxLength is enforced. Unauthenticated remote clients negotiating permessage-deflate can send highly compressible messages, forcing processIncomingMessage() to allocate excessive memory and crash the server process.
msgpackr before 2.1.4 Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity via UnpackrStream and decodeIter

msgpackr before 2.1.4 contains an inefficient algorithmic complexity vulnerability that allows remote attackers to cause denial of service by repeatedly re-decoding buffered incomplete values. Attackers can stream a large container of small elements in small chunks to UnpackrStream or decodeIter, triggering quadratic decoding cost that blocks the Node.js event loop.
diaspora* before 0.10.0 HTML Injection via Inviter Name in Invitation Emails

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in Notifier#invite that allows authenticated users to inject HTML or markdown into invitation emails through unescaped profile names. Attackers can set profile first or last names containing raw HTML, links, or images so invitation emails sent from the pod render spoofed content in recipients' mail clients.
diaspora* before 0.10.0 Path Traversal via Account Import Photos Archive

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a path traversal (zip slip) vulnerability in ImportService#unzip_photos_file that allows authenticated users to write files outside the extraction folder. Attackers can upload a crafted photos zip archive during account import with ../ entry names to create new files at arbitrary locations writable by the diaspora* process.
OpenOLAT 20.2.2 before 20.3.12, 21.0.7, and 21.1.2 Missing Authentication via notifyResult

OpenOLAT 20.2.2 before 20.3.12, 21.0.0 before 21.0.7, and 21.1.0 before 21.1.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the TranscodingDeliveryDispatcher notifyResult callback endpoint. Unauthenticated attackers can POST crafted TranscoderJobResult JSON with attacker-supplied URLs to overwrite transcoded video and audio files and force server-side requests.
Gogs before 0.14.4 Path Equivalence Bypass via NTFS .git Aliases

Gogs before 0.14.4 on Windows contains a path equivalence vulnerability in isRepositoryGitPath that allows authenticated users with write access to bypass .git directory protection using NTFS aliases. Attackers can create, rename or upload files via aliases like git~1 or .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION to overwrite .git/config or hooks and execute commands as the Gogs process.
Reposilite 3.5.27 before 3.6.7 Brute-Force Protection Bypass via X-Forwarded-For

Reposilite 3.5.27 before 3.6.7 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to evade login bans by spoofing the X-Forwarded-For header. Attackers can rotate the header value to make unlimited password or token guesses, or forge failed attempts to lock out legitimate clients.
Opencast before 20.6 Path Traversal via Workspace File Resolution

Opencast before 20.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in WorkspaceImpl.toWorkspaceFile that allows authenticated ingest users to write files outside the workspace root via unvalidated element paths. Attackers can submit media packages whose element URIs or identifiers contain ../ sequences, causing Workspace.get to create directories and write fetched content with Opencast process privileges.
Zipline before 4.8.3 Server-Side Request Forgery via OIDC Avatar URL

Zipline before 4.8.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated OIDC users to make the server fetch arbitrary URLs via the userinfo picture claim. Attackers who control their picture claim at the identity provider can force fetchToDataURL() to request internal or cloud-metadata URLs and read responses from their stored avatar.
Portainer 2.39.0 before 2.39.9, 2.40.0 before 2.45.4, and 3.0.0 before 3.1.0 Authorization Bypass via WebSocket Attach and Exec

Portainer 2.39.0 before 2.39.9, 2.40.0 before 2.45.4, and 3.0.0 before 3.1.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows Standard users to access other users' containers via the WebSocket attach and exec endpoints. Attackers with shared environment access can use leaked container or exec IDs to hijack sessions over /api/websocket/attach or /api/websocket/exec, gaining interactive root shells.
DBHub before 1.7.0 Read-Only Mode Bypass via Backslash-Escaped Quotes

DBHub before 1.7.0 contains a read-only mode bypass vulnerability that allows MCP clients restricted to readonly execute_sql to run write and DDL statements via backslash-escaped quotes. Attackers can hide stacked statements that clear transaction_read_only or COMMIT inside strings misparsed by scanSingleQuotedString, letting them modify or drop MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL data.
VoidAuth before 1.19.2 ProxyAuth Access Control Bypass via Encoded Path Separators

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to evade stricter ProxyAuth domain rules by sending percent-encoded path separators. Attackers can request paths with encoded slashes, backslashes, semicolons, or dot segments that match a broader rule, reaching restricted paths once the reverse proxy or backend decodes them.
VoidAuth before 1.19.2 Stale Email Verification Status via PATCH /email

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an improper verification vulnerability that allows authenticated users to retain the emailVerified flag by changing their email address while EMAIL_VERIFICATION is disabled. Attackers with a previously verified account can set another person's address via the PATCH /email handler, receiving OIDC email_verified=true claims to impersonate that owner in relying applications.
VoidAuth before 1.19.2 Insufficient Session Expiration via Passkey Account Recovery

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because the POST /reset_password/passkey/end handler never calls endUserSessions(). Attackers holding a stolen session cookie keep authenticated access to the victim's account even after the victim recovers it by registering a new passkey.
ByteStash 1.5.0 before 1.6.1 Login CSRF via OIDC Callback

ByteStash 1.5.0 before 1.6.1 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the /api/auth/oidc/callback handler because OIDC state is not bound to the initiating browser. Attackers can start an OIDC login with their own account and lure victims into opening the withheld callback URL, logging them into the attacker's account to read saved snippets.
Donetick through 0.1.86 SSRF via Circle Webhook and Discord Notification URLs

Donetick through 0.1.86 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows self-registered users to make the server send requests by setting unvalidated circle webhook or Discord notification URLs. Attackers can point these URLs at loopback or internal services, causing EventsProducer and the Discord notifier to POST partly attacker-influenced bodies to internal network hosts.
Donetick before 0.1.86 Path Traversal via Profile Image Field

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to delete other users' files by storing a crafted image value via PUT /api/v1/users. Attackers can set their image to a traversal key and upload a new profile photo, causing storage.Delete to remove other users' attachments or photos under the storage root.
Donetick before 0.1.86 Path Traversal via AssetHandler

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the GET /api/v1/assets/*filepath route that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass URL signature checks by prefixing paths with profiles/. Attackers who know a private upload's storage key can request profiles/../users/<id>/<uuid>.<ext> to retrieve private attachments without a signature or login.
graphql-core 3.2.12 before 3.2.14 and 3.3.0rc1 before 3.3.2 Denial of Service via Parser max_tokens Comment Runs

graphql-core 3.2.12 before 3.2.14 and 3.3.0rc1 before 3.3.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the parser max_tokens limit using long runs of comments. Attackers can submit GraphQL documents of consecutive comments that Lexer.lookahead fully tokenizes before limit checks, consuming CPU and memory proportional to document size.
HedgeDoc before 1.12.1 Prototype Pollution via Note History API

HedgeDoc before 1.12.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the POST /history/:noteId endpoint that allows authenticated users to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ as the noteId. Attackers can send a pinned value to /history/__proto__, which historyPost() in lib/history.js assigns onto the prototype, crashing the Node.js process and causing denial of service for all users.
Electerm before 5.9.0 OS Command Injection via Unicode Quotes in PowerShell

Electerm before 5.9.0 on Windows contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute PowerShell code via crafted file or folder names containing Unicode quote characters. Attackers can deliver names containing U+2019 through archives, WSL distributions, or SMB shares, which break out of getFolderSizeWin() and calcLocal() quoting when victims request folder sizes, executing code as the electerm user.
Kirby 5.0.0 before 5.6.4 XSS via Chunked Upload Race Condition

Kirby 5.0.0 before 5.6.4 contains a race condition in Kirby\Api\Upload::processChunk() that allows authenticated users with upload permission to bypass SVG sanitization. Attackers can race concurrent chunked uploads sharing a filename to swap a benign SVG with a script-bearing SVG, executing stored cross-site scripting in the site origin.
Ground Station before 0.8.25 Path Traversal via SatDump post_process_pipeline

Ground Station before 0.8.25 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator operators to write files outside data/decoded via the post_process_pipeline value. Attackers can insert ../ sequences into a scheduled observation's IQ task configuration so SatDump creates directories, overwrites same-named files, and recursively deletes created trees on failure.
FreeRDP before 3.33.1 Use-After-Free via WinPR LinkedList Enumerator

FreeRDP before 3.33.1 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the WinPR wLinkedList collection because LinkedList_FreeNode() frees nodes without updating the cached list->current enumerator pointer. When calling code removes the node the enumerator references, LinkedList_Enumerator_MoveNext() or LinkedList_Enumerator_Current() reads freed heap memory, which can crash the process.
ntop nDPI through 6.0 Out-of-Bounds Read via ndpi_serializer_get_buffer

ntop nDPI through 6.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read and unsigned length underflow in ndpi_serializer_get_buffer() in src/lib/ndpi_serializer.c when stripping leading NUL and space bytes. Buffers holding only spaces or NULs, or a used length of 0 set through ndpi_serializer_set_buffer_len(), cause reads past the heap buffer or a wrapped 4294967295 length, crashing the embedding application.
libical before 4.0.7 Double Free via icalparser_clean

libical before 4.0.7 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in icalparser_clean() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying truncated iCalendar input. Attackers can provide an iCalendar file or stream missing a matching END line, causing the returned component to be freed twice and crashing applications.
wfuzz through 3.1.1 Stored XSS via HTML Report Printer

Wfuzz through 3.1.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious target servers to inject script by returning crafted links written unescaped into HTML reports. When the links script and html printer are used, attacker-supplied href values close the unquoted anchor tag and execute JavaScript when the operator opens the report.
anacrolix/torrent before 1.63.0 Improper Certificate Validation via HTTPS Tracker Client

Anacrolix torrent before 1.63.0 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in NewClient within tracker/http/client.go, which unconditionally sets InsecureSkipVerify to true for HTTPS trackers. Attackers able to intercept tracker traffic can impersonate trackers with any certificate, observe info_hash and peer_id values, and return forged peer lists.
Portainer 2.39.0 before 2.45.1 SSRF via Multiple Outbound-Request Features

Portainer Community Edition and Business Edition 2.39.0 before 2.45.1 contain a server-side request forgery vulnerability because user-supplied URLs are only syntax-checked by validate.IsURL without resolved address validation. Authenticated users can abuse Git cloning, Helm retrieval, registry ping, or the GitLab proxy to reach loopback, internal, and cloud metadata addresses, probing ports and reading responses.
better-chatbot before 2.0.0 Missing Authorization via Manual Tool Mode Built-in Tools

better-chatbot before 2.0.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that lets built-in tools run without user confirmation in Manual tool mode, because src/app/api/chat/route.ts keeps their execute handlers. Attackers can plant prompt-injected documents or web pages that make the HTTP request tool send conversation data to attacker-controlled URLs.
anacrolix/torrent before 1.62.0 Denial of Service via Bencode Decoder Recursion

anacrolix/torrent before 1.62.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in Decoder.readOneValue in bencode/decode.go that allows attackers to crash the process by supplying deeply nested bencode data. Attackers can deliver crafted .torrent files or magnet link metadata with millions of nested lists to cause a fatal stack overflow, or deeply nested v2 file trees to exhaust CPU.
dsniff through 2.5a2 Integer Underflow Out-of-Bounds Write via decode_sniffer()

dsniff through 2.5a2 contains an integer underflow in decode_sniffer() in decode_sniffer.c that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write past the global obuf buffer. Attackers can send a UDP datagram to port 2001 on a monitored segment with a 4096-byte string, disabling base64_pton bounds checks to corrupt memory and crash dsniff.
WPGSI: Spreadsheet Integration before 3.8.5 CSRF via Show Delete Action

WPGSI: Spreadsheet Integration before 3.8.5 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to delete posts by abusing the delete action in wpgsi_show_view() without nonce verification. Attackers can trick a logged-in administrator into following a crafted wpgsi-show link with action=delete and an id parameter to delete arbitrary posts or pages.
Members WordPress Plugin before 3.3.1 Missing Authorization via Latest Posts Block

Members WordPress plugin before 3.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to read role-restricted posts by viewing Latest Posts blocks in full-content mode. The block renders raw post_content without firing the_content filter, bypassing members_content_permissions_protect() and exposing complete bodies of restricted posts.
Members WordPress Plugin before 3.3.1 Missing Authorization via Latest Comments Block

Members WordPress plugin before 3.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to read comments on role-restricted posts via the Latest Comments block. Attackers can view pages hosting the block, where get_the_ID() checks the host page and get_comment_excerpt() bypasses filtering, exposing restricted comments, post titles, and links.
Members WordPress Plugin before 3.3.1 Denial of Service via Block Permissions Message Attribute

MemberPress Members before 3.3.1, with the Block Permissions add-on enabled, contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated Author-level users to crash pages by saving a non-string blockPermissionsMessage block attribute. Attackers can store a JSON array in the attribute so wpautop() in get_block_replacement_content() throws a PHP 8 TypeError, causing fatal errors on post, home, search, and REST pages for unauthorized viewers.
Members WordPress Plugin 3.2.28 before 3.3.2 Private Site Authentication Bypass

Members WordPress plugin by MemberPress 3.2.28 before 3.3.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to evade Private Site mode via login page exemption. Attackers can request the front-end login path with a pagename query variable to make WordPress render hidden published pages or the full blog index.
itsourcecode Event Management System booking.php cross site scripting

A vulnerability has been found in itsourcecode Event Management System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file booking.php. Such manipulation of the argument venue_id leads to cross site scripting. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.
Open Asset Import Library Assimp ASE File Importer ASELoader.cpp InternReadFile out-of-bounds write

A flaw has been found in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.5. This affects the function ASEImporter::InternReadFile of the file code/AssetLib/ASE/ASELoader.cpp of the component ASE File Importer. This manipulation causes out-of-bounds write. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 6.0.6 mitigates this issue. Patch name: 7ccc44a338dcdcc81023484388126ab1a8250e94. You should upgrade the affected component.
itsourcecode Insurance Management System insertClient.php sql injection

A vulnerability was detected in itsourcecode Insurance Management System 1.0. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file /insertClient.php. The manipulation of the argument client_id results in sql injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used.
xuxueli xxl-job Group Management JobGroupController.java update cross-site request forgery

A security vulnerability has been detected in xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. The affected element is the function insert/update of the file admin/src/main/java/com/xxl/job/admin/business/controller/JobGroupController.java of the component Group Management. The manipulation of the argument addressList leads to cross-site request forgery. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
OpenShot Video Editor through 4.1.1 Deserialization via Legacy Project Import

OpenShot Video Editor (openshot-qt) through 4.1.1 contains an unsafe deserialization vulnerability in ProjectDataStore.load() and read_legacy_project_file() that passes non-JSON project files to pickle.load() without restriction. Attackers can trick users into opening a crafted .osp project file containing a pickle __reduce__ gadget to execute code with the user's privileges.
libexpat through 2.10.0 Isolated High Surrogate via UTF-16 Conversion

libexpat through 2.10.0 contains an improper Unicode handling vulnerability in DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16 conversion functions in xmltok.c that can split valid surrogate pairs when output space is limited. In XML_UNICODE builds parsing non-native byte order UTF-16 input, attackers can supply crafted documents that deliver lone high surrogates to character data and default handlers.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Type Confusion via Curve2D point Field

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in curve2d_check_changes() that casts a Curve2D point field node to M_Coordinate2D without type checking. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/BIFS scene placing another node type such as LinearGradient in that field, causing an invalid pointer read that crashes the process.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in xmt_resolve_od_links via Discarded SceneReplace Subtree

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_node_end() that leaves freed child node MFURL fields in the OD link list. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with an extra top-level SceneReplace node, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory, crashing MP4Box and corrupting the heap.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_node_unregister via PROTO Nodes

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that allows scene commands to reference PROTO sub-graph nodes freed by a scene replace command. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file that causes gf_node_get_field() and gf_node_unregister() to access freed memory, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting heap memory.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Heap Buffer Over-read via Text fontStyle Type Confusion

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in src/compositor/mpeg4_text.c that allows heap out-of-bounds reads by casting a Text node's fontStyle field to M_FontStyle unchecked. Attackers can craft an XMT/BIFS scene placing a smaller node like Face in fontStyle, causing build_text to read past the allocation and crash MP4Box.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Type Confusion in ctxload_process via XMT ODUpdate

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in ctxload_process() in src/filters/load_bt_xmt.c that casts object descriptor update entries without checking the descriptor tag. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/BT scene placing a different descriptor type in a GF_ODUpdate command, causing gf_list_get() to dereference an invalid pointer and crash MP4Box.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference in gf_sg_command_apply via Replace Command Without Payload

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_sg_proto_del via XMT PROTO Delete

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Out-of-Bounds Read in avilib via AVI Audio Tracks

Gammapy through 2.1 Code Injection via WCSSHAPE FITS Header Card

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference in gf_sg_proto_create_node

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_node_unregister via XMT DEF Lookup

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability because xmt_find_node() in loader_xmt.c resolves DEF names without verifying the node belongs to the current scene graph. GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_event_target_get_node

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference in Compositor Node Handlers

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference via JSScript_LoadVRML

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in JSScript_LoadVRML() in src/scenegraph/vrml_js.c that reads unchecked script_text pointers of Script node url entries. GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in ctxload_process via InputSensor Stream

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference in gf_sg_command_apply via MFNode Field Replace Without Value

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() in src/scenegraph/commands.c when handling MFNode field replace commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with an MFNode field replace command lacking a node value to crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Type Confusion in gf_sg_command_apply MFNode Field Replace

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that misinterprets single node values as child lists for MFNode field replace commands. GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in load_xmt_done

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in load_xmt_done() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that reads freed nodes during XMT parser teardown. GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in xmt_resolve_od_links via SFNode Replacement

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that leaves freed node URL fields in the pending object descriptor link list after SFNode replacement. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that reassigns a single-node field, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory, crashing the process and potentially corrupting the heap.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Uncontrolled Recursion via xmt_remove_od_links_recursive

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in xmt_remove_od_links_recursive() in loader_xmt.c that lacks any depth limit when walking node children. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with deeply nested or cyclic node and SFCommandBuffer references to exhaust the stack and crash MP4Box on import.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via gf_sg_proto_del

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in scene graph teardown that allows attackers to trigger access to freed memory via crafted scene files. A node shared across multiple PROTO node_code lists is freed by gf_sg_reset(), and gf_sg_proto_del() then calls gf_node_unregister() on the dangling pointer, crashing MP4Box.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Uncontrolled Recursion via gf_sg_proto_instantiate

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_instantiate() in src/scenegraph/vrml_proto.c that lacks cycle detection or depth limits. Attackers can craft an XMT scene whose PROTO body instantiates itself directly or indirectly, exhausting the stack and crashing MP4Box when imported.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference in TraverseForm

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in TraverseForm() in src/compositor/mpeg4_form.c due to an off-by-one groupsIndex bounds check. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with a Form node having constraints but an empty groupsIndex field to crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.
WeddingShare through 1.8.2 Missing Authorization via MediaViewer GalleryItem

WeddingShare through 1.8.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the anonymous MediaViewerController.GalleryItem action that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve item upload paths without the gallery secret key. Attackers can enumerate sequential integer item ids to learn paths and uploader names, then download photos and videos from key-protected galleries served as static files.
freedit before 0.9.9 Authorization Bypass in Post Editing via Private Inn

Freedit before 0.9.9 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the edit_post_post handler for POST /post/edit/:pid that skips ownership and status checks when a Private inn is submitted. Members of a Private inn can overwrite any post by sequential id, including moderator-locked posts, re-attributing it to themselves and destroying original content.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in xmt_resolve_od_links via Discarded Out-of-Scope Node

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to access freed heap memory via stale object descriptor links. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene where xmt_node_end() frees a subtree containing InputSensor MFURL fields, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory and crash MP4Box.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_odm_disconnect

Servas before 1.2.0 Missing Authorization in Tag, Link, and Group Controllers

Servas before 1.2.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to modify and delete other users' data by supplying target resource ids. Attackers can abuse TagController update and destroy, LinkController destroy, and GroupController destroy actions to rename or delete tags and delete links and groups.
freedit before 0.9.9 Authorization Bypass via Inn Moderation Routes

Attackers can supply their own inn id with a foreign post or comment id to lock or hide content instance-wide, or pin private posts to expose titles.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in xmt_resolve_od_links via Stale URL Segment Pointer

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Uncontrolled Recursion via xmt_discard_subtree

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in xmt_discard_subtree() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to exhaust the call stack. Attackers can persuade a user to process a crafted XMT file with deeply nested discarded SFNode and MFNode fields to crash MP4Box.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via Discarded XMT Nodes

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT-A scene loader that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted XMT files. Attackers can persuade a user to process an XMT file whose discarded out-of-scope nodes cause gf_node_unregister() to dereference a freed child, crashing the process.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via xmt_node_end

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_node_end() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that writes to freed heap memory when replacing single-node field commands. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file where a Conditional node owning the command is unregistered, corrupting heap memory and crashing MP4Box.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Heap Buffer Over-read in gf_xml_sax_peek_node

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in XMT Loader

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Stack Buffer Overflow via xmt_resolve_od_links

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via xmt_text_content

Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file whose text content makes xmt_text_content() pass the freed node to gf_node_get_tag(), reading freed heap memory and crashing MP4Box.
GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_node_get_name via XMT Parser

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference via MPEG-4 Sensor Handling

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_sg_command_new via XMT Loader

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Double Free via gf_sg_sfcommand_del

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference in gf_odf_encode_ui_config

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Type Confusion via xmt_parse_command

OpenAirInterface CN5G AMF before 2.2.2 Stale PDU Session Contexts via SMF Selection Failure

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 Orphaned CHF Charging Sessions via HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate

OpenAirInterface CN5G PCF through 2.2.2 Memory Leak via SM Policy Deletion

Event Tickets Manager for WooCommerce 1.5.4 - 1.6.1 - Unauthenticated Cross-Product Ticket Price Manipulation

The Event Tickets Manager for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 1.6.2 does not check that the ticket type and price chosen through one of its unauthenticated AJAX actions belong to the event ticket later added to the cart, and stores them site-wide, allowing unauthenticated visitors to buy an event ticket at the lower ticket-type price configured on a different event.
Front Editor < 5.1.0 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Uploaded File Content-Type Sniffing

The Front User Submit WordPress plugin before 5.1.0 does not validate the content of files uploaded through one of its unauthenticated endpoints and later serves them back with a Content-Type derived from the file's bytes and an inline disposition, allowing unauthenticated attackers to store an HTML or SVG payload and obtain a same-origin URL that executes arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who opens it, including an administrator.
Yoast SEO < 28.9 - Unauthenticated Private Content Disclosure via Headless REST Head Endpoint

The Yoast SEO WordPress plugin before 28.9 does not check that content is publicly viewable before returning its SEO metadata through a public REST endpoint, allowing unauthenticated users who know or can guess the URL of a private post, page or custom post type item to read its title, author, publication date and an excerpt of its content.

Mooberry Book Manager <= 4.16.2 - Subscriber+ Book Buy-Link Rewrite via mbdb_update_apple_books_links

The Mooberry Book Manager WordPress plugin through 4.16.2 does not perform a capability check on one of its AJAX actions and protects it only with a nonce that it outputs to every authenticated user on all admin pages, allowing any logged-in user, including Subscribers, to trigger a site-wide rewrite of stored book purchase links and change a related Mooberry Book Manager WordPress plugin through 4.16.2 option.
Mooberry Book Manager <= 4.16.2 - Subscriber+ Book Publisher Update via bulk_quick_save_bulk_edit

The Mooberry Book Manager WordPress plugin through 4.16.2 does not perform any capability or nonce check in one of its AJAX actions, allowing any authenticated user with a minimal role such as Subscriber to change the publisher assigned to any book, including books created by other users, and to create new book records. The missing nonce check also makes the action exploitable via CSRF against any logged-in user.
Asset CleanUp: Page Speed Booster < 1.4.0.7 - Unauthenticated CORS Misconfiguration via Reflected Origin with Credentials

The Asset CleanUp: Page Speed Booster WordPress plugin before 1.4.0.7 does not restrict which origins it reflects into its cross-origin resource sharing response headers and pairs the reflected origin with credentialed access, allowing a page on a related origin to read a logged-in user's authenticated content across origins.
SMS Alert < 4.0.4 - Admin+ SQLi via 'ID' Parameter
The SMS Alert WordPress plugin before 4.0.4 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, leading to SQL injection exploitable by administrators.
LifterLMS < 10.0.5 - Subscriber+ Quiz Question Disclosure via query_quiz_questions

The LifterLMS WordPress plugin before 10.0.5 does not perform a capability or nonce check in one of its quiz-question query AJAX handlers, allowing any authenticated user with subscriber-level access to enumerate the titles of all published quiz questions, including those for courses they are not enrolled in.

Skyvern-AI Skyvern browser_egress_policy.py classify_url server-side request forgery

The manipulation results in server-side request forgery. The attack may be performed from remote. Upgrading to version 1.0.57 is sufficient to fix this issue. Web-Token jwt-framework before 3.4.10 DoS via Unbounded PBES2 p2c Iteration Count

Web-Token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.10, 4.0.0 before 4.0.7, and 4.1.0 before 4.1.7 contain an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in PBES2AESKW::unwrapKey(), which passes the attacker-controlled p2c JWE header value to hash_pbkdf2() without an upper bound. Unauthenticated attackers can send a JWE using a PBES2-HS*+A*KW algorithm with a huge p2c iteration count to force lengthy PBKDF2 computations and exhaust server CPU.
web-token jwt-framework 1.2.0 before 3.4.10 Missing Authentication in Chacha20Poly1305 Key Encryption

web-token jwt-framework 1.2.0 before 3.4.10, jwt-experimental before 3.4.10, 4.0.x before 4.0.7, and 4.1.x before 4.1.7 contain a missing integrity check in the experimental Chacha20Poly1305 key-encryption algorithm, which discards the Poly1305 tag in encryptKey() and calls openssl_decrypt() without it in decryptKey(). Attackers on the token path can modify the encrypted content encryption key undetected.
web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.10 RSA1_5 Bleichenbacher Padding Oracle

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.10, 4.0.x before 4.0.7, and 4.1.x before 4.1.7 contain a padding oracle in RSACrypt::decryptWithRSA15() because RSA1_5 decryption lacks implicit rejection, so invalid padding, wrong CEK length, and valid padding take measurably different time. Remote attackers can submit adaptively crafted JWE encrypted_key values and measure these timing differences to recover the wrapped content encryption key.
web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.12 ECDH-ES Weak Key Derivation via ConcatKDF

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.12, 4.0.x before 4.0.8, 4.1.x before 4.1.10, and 4.2.x before 4.2.4, and jwt-encryption-algorithm-ecdh-es through 3.2.10, have a ConcatKDF::generate() that performs a single SHA-256 round, deriving at most 32 bytes for ECDH-ES and ECDH-SS direct key agreement. Anyone holding a JWE using A256CBC-HS512 can decrypt it under an all-zero AES key, while A192CBC-HS384 content keys have only 64-bit strength.
Hysteria 2.5.0 before 2.8.2 QUIC Packet OOM via Sniff Crypto Length

Hysteria 2.5.0 before 2.8.2 contains a memory allocation vulnerability when sniffing is enabled, allowing authenticated users to trigger out-of-memory conditions. Attackers with a valid password can forward a crafted QUIC packet with a huge crypto length, causing the server to exhaust memory and crash.
Hysteria 2.5.0 before 2.9.2 Denial of Service via HTTP Sniff Header

Hysteria 2.5.0 before 2.9.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the HTTP sniff implementation that fails to limit header size. Attackers can continuously send excessively large HTTP headers without terminating them, exhausting server memory and causing out-of-memory crashes.
Hysteria 1.0.0 before 2.9.2 Denial of Service via max_datagram_frame_size

Hysteria 1.0.0 before 2.9.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in FragUDPMessage where UDP fragmentation fails to handle headers larger than the maximum datagram payload size. Authenticated clients can advertise a small max_datagram_frame_size and trigger a UDP response, causing a slice bounds panic that crashes the server.
Hysteria 2.0.0 before 2.9.2 UDP ACL Bypass Enabling SSRF

Hysteria from 2.0.0 before 2.9.2 contains an ACL bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clients to reach blocked UDP destinations by reusing an established UDP session. Attackers can open a session to an allowed destination, then send later packets to localhost or private-network addresses to access internal-only UDP services.
Dockhand before 1.0.50 Improper RBAC Enforcement via API Endpoints

Dockhand before 1.0.50 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows authenticated unprivileged users to read restricted data by querying API endpoints lacking RBAC checks. Attackers can access /api/users, /api/license, and /api/hawser/connect to obtain user emails and roles, the full license key, and environment details, while an invalid license grants all users admin rights.
Dockhand before 1.0.57 RCE via PATH Poisoning in Stack Deploy

Dockhand before 1.0.57 merges stack secret environment variables into the environment used to spawn docker compose during stack deploys without filtering reserved keys such as PATH. An authenticated attacker with stacks:edit permission can set PATH to a directory containing a malicious binary and trigger a deploy, executing arbitrary commands as the Dockhand server process user.
Dockhand before 1.0.57 Privilege Escalation via OIDC Provider Update Handler

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows non-admin users with settings:edit permission to modify OIDC provider configuration due to an improper permission check. Attackers can send a PUT request to /api/auth/oidc/<provider-id> setting adminClaim to their own OIDC group, gaining full admin access on their next OIDC login.
Dockhand before 1.0.57 Clickjacking via Missing Frame Protection Headers

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a clickjacking vulnerability because src/hooks.server.ts never sets X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors headers on responses. Attackers on a same-site origin can embed the UI in an invisible iframe to trick authenticated users into stopping stacks, deleting resources, or changing settings.
Dockhand before 1.0.57 Cross-Site Request Forgery via Missing Origin Validation

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to perform state-changing actions by exploiting missing Origin header validation and absent CSRF tokens. Attackers can lure authenticated users to a same-site attacker page that submits forged POST requests to stop, start, or delete stacks, modify settings, and change credentials.
Finsys Dockhand 1.0.7 before 1.0.57 Path Traversal via Stack env/raw Endpoint

Finsys Dockhand 1.0.7 before 1.0.57 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows low-privileged users to read and write arbitrary files by setting an unvalidated envPath on a stack source. Attackers with stacks:edit permission can point envPath to files like /etc/shadow or SSH keys, then use GET or PUT on /api/stacks/[name]/env/raw to read or overwrite them.
ERPNext 15.8.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization Exposes Transaction Child Table Rows

Frappe ERPNext 15.8.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an endpoint shared across modules that returns transaction child table rows without checking permissions on the child table or parent document. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can supply document types and filter conditions to read business document line details and probe record values.
Frappe ERPNext before 15.124.2 Missing Authorization in Accounts Clearance Date Endpoint

Frappe ERPNext before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that records bank clearance dates, which checks only a broad role permission before writing to caller-named payment documents. Authenticated Accounts Users can send crafted requests naming payment documents of other companies, outside their User Permissions, or already submitted, to alter clearance dates and compromise bank reconciliation integrity.
Frappe ERPNext 16.0.0 before 16.36.0 Missing Authorization in Manufacturing Stock Reservation Cancellation

Frappe ERPNext 16.0.0 before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Manufacturing module endpoint that allows authenticated users to cancel Stock Reservation Entries without record-level write permission. Low-privilege attackers can send crafted requests naming manufacturing documents of other companies or outside their User Permissions to release reserved stock and disrupt stock allocation.
Frappe ERPNext before 15.124.2 Missing Authorization Across Endpoints and Reports

Frappe ERPNext before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.53.0 fails to enforce record-level authorization in several endpoints, reports and forms, allowing authenticated low-privilege users to access data beyond their role. Attackers can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other companies' financial, stock, pricing and contact data or make constrained changes to those records.
Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Import Endpoint

Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module import endpoint that does not check whether the caller may create inserted records or download a named file. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted import requests to read file contents and create Serial No and Batch records.
Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.122.0 SQL Injection via Sort Parameters

Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in endpoints that build part of a query from caller-supplied sort parameters without validation. Authenticated low-privilege users can send crafted requests whose sort parameter holds SQL that the database executes as part of the query, extracting sensitive information.
Frappe ERPNext 12.0.0 before 15.121.4 Unauthorized Private File Read in Accounts Module

Frappe ERPNext 12.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns the parsed content of private import-format files without checking permission on the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read those private files.
Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in CRM and Support Communications

Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a CRM and Support module endpoint that returns Communications of documents without checking whether the caller may read them. Authenticated attackers with a common operational role can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read their email communications and relink them away from their original documents.
Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Item Records

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns Item master records without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to retrieve complete item data including costing and purchase rates.
Frappe ERPNext 15.53.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Assets Module Endpoint

Frappe ERPNext 15.53.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Assets module endpoint that returns cost and quantity fields of purchase and stock transactions without record-level permission checks. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read these fields.
Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Accounts Module Endpoint

Frappe ERPNext 15.x 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns Sales Order and Purchase Order values and counterparties without checking permissions on the requested records. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read their order values and counterparties.
Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Valuation Rates

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns item valuation rates without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to retrieve their valuation rates.
Frappe ERPNext 8.2.5 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Endpoint

Frappe ERPNext 8.2.5 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns on-hand stock quantities without checking record-level permissions. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming restricted records to disclose stock quantities and confirm item existence.
Frappe ERPNext 6.26.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Quantity Endpoint

Frappe ERPNext 6.26.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns stock data without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read per-warehouse and company-wide stock quantities and confirm item existence.
Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization Exposes POS Opening Entries
